audit.finding: One shared process seam is assessed; no alternate SWAP kernel or use-case-specific SNOW implementation is introduced.
Candidate SNOW process has no file/path/parsing I/O; F-VQ adds only qualification fixtures and tooling.
Parameters, persistent state, forcing, result/flux and diagnostics are explicit separate types.
Persistent SNOW continuation state is limited to total snow water storage and retained liquid-water substate; reporting history is excluded.
Legacy algebraic intermediates remain local workspace and are not persisted per column.
F-VQ16 introduces no storage-layout restriction that prevents SoA/pools/batches.
Evaluation leaves committed input state unchanged, replay is bit-exact, and accepted continuation is reproducible. F-KT remains transaction authority; no separate transaction engine is introduced.
Same committed state plus forcing replays bit-exactly; no hidden process warm-start state exists.

Interface exposes generic t0/t1 and accepts a non-midnight one-day interval, but scientific validity is deliberately restricted to one legacy Snow(2) call of exact duration 1.0. No arbitrary-duration claim is made.
No coupling-window policy is changed; downstream composition must schedule the admitted daily SNOW event without redefining its physics.
No coupling contract is modified.
Groundwater interface contract is not touched by this process-only qualification.

For every admitted reference call the unrounded snow-component identity closes exactly to the same floating-point result as B1.10. Melt is a snow-storage outflow but must be booked as an internal transfer when received by surface/soil; F-VQ16 does not claim whole-system F-KT completeness.
No groundwater response tangent is involved.
No coupling-run cost policy is changed.
Process data ownership is compatible with MultiSWAP, but F-VQ16 does not admit any SNOW MultiSWAP runtime composition.
No tile-to-MODFLOW cardinality assumption is introduced.
Deep-vadose transfer is unaffected.
No component-transition storage transfer is changed.
SNOW process is independent of a specific soil-water solver implementation.
B1.10 SNOW physics is reused without introducing a duplicate alternative physics path.
SNOW process does not access HeadCalc internals.
No numerical execution policy changes or silently modifies SNOW physics.
No fallback or bounded-cost policy is introduced.
Exact compiled B1.10 source is the reference oracle; no reduced-accuracy replacement is admitted.
Candidate exposes explicit status and snow mass diagnostics; F-VQ evidence records the exact tested route and holds.
Candidate defines only compact SNOW state; inactive allocation remains runtime-owned and was not scientifically broadened here.
No tile, transfer-zone or system-composition ownership is moved into the SNOW process.
No midnight, file-format or MODFLOW dependency is introduced. The only retained temporal restriction is explicitly source-qualified one-call B1.10 duration semantics.
This audit explicitly records the invariant assessment for the scientific admission change.
